cards.audience: Thought leaders and content creators worried about AI erasing their voice
cards.tag: If you are a thought leader watching AI summarize your work
cards.prompt: I just read an argument that AEO rewards insight over signal — specifically that AI agents can collect information but cannot generate the interpretation that comes from lived expertise. I've been building thought leadership content for [X years] in [my space]. Help me audit my last five pieces of content and identify where I'm producing signal that could be synthesized away versus insight that's irreducibly mine. What questions should I be asking to find the difference?

cards.audience: Founders building content strategy for their company or personal brand
cards.tag: If you are a founder investing in content and wondering if it still works
cards.prompt: I read a post arguing that the shortcut era in content is over — that AI synthesis now rewards depth, specificity, and real positions over volume and optimization. I'm a founder at [business stage] building content for [audience]. Based on this framework, help me identify where my current content strategy is built for ranking rather than citability, and what it would look like to rebuild it around genuine insight and AEO principles.

cards.audience: Agency owners and content strategists advising clients on AI-era strategy
cards.tag: If you are an agency or strategist advising clients on content in the AI era
cards.prompt: I'm reading about a methodology called PRISM that reframes content strategy around four dimensions: AEO citability, personalization, synthesis, and guided inquiry. I work with clients who are still optimizing for traditional SEO metrics. Help me build a simple diagnostic conversation I can use with clients to assess where their content strategy is misaligned with how AI agents are now selecting and synthesizing sources — and how to frame the shift without losing them.

cards.audience: Readers exploring AI tools who want to make content personally actionable
cards.tag: If you are someone who reads good content but struggles to apply it to your situation
cards.prompt: I just read a post that describes the gap between information and meaning — the idea that even useful content fails because it can't connect to a reader's specific situation without a structured bridge. I'm a [role] dealing with [current challenge]. Using the ideas in this post about personalization and guided inquiry, help me turn the core arguments into a set of questions I can use to filter this thinking through my actual context and figure out what it means for what I'm doing right now.

cards.audience: Web3 and token-gated community builders thinking about member engagement
cards.tag: If you are building a community or collective in the Web3 or creator economy
cards.prompt: I read an argument that authentic community relationships — where members are stakeholders and builders, not just audience — function as literal technical signal in an AI-mediated world because depth of engagement shows up in how agents reason about a creator's work. I'm building a community at [stage] around [focus area]. Help me think through what 'stakeholder not subscriber' looks like structurally in my community, and how genuine engagement could function as a long-term content infrastructure advantage rather than just a values choice.

cards.audience: Any reader who wants to apply this framework to their own specific situation
cards.tag: If you want to think this through for your own context
cards.prompt: I just read a piece arguing that AEO is fundamentally different from SEO because it rewards irreducible insight over optimized signal — and that thought leaders who take real positions, build real depth, and create conditions for genuine reader personalization will be the ones whose work survives AI synthesis. Here's my situation: [describe your role, what you create or publish, who your audience is, and what your biggest content challenge is right now]. Given all of that, where should I start, and what does this framework actually mean for me?
